# ksjdata

<!-- badges: start -->
[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/UchidaMizuki/ksjdata/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/UchidaMizuki/ksjdata/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)
<!-- badges: end -->

English | [日本語](README.ja.md)

ksjdata provides National Land Numerical Information (国土数値情報, KSJ), published by the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure, Transport and Tourism of Japan.

- `ksj_available` is the catalog: it lists every supported file, with its dataset, release, area, and the page of its dataset. Filter it to choose files.
- `ksj_get()` downloads and reads one file, and returns one layer as an `sf` tibble. To get several files, iterate over their names, for example with `purrr::map()`. Each file is cached by the [tarchives](https://github.com/UchidaMizuki/tarchives) package, so it is downloaded only once.
- Columns are named in Japanese after the official attribute table. Use `col_names = "raw"` to keep the names of the file (usually attribute codes such as `N03_001`), for example for older releases.

## Installation

You can install the development version of ksjdata from GitHub with:

``` r
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("UchidaMizuki/ksjdata")
```

## Usage

Filter `ksj_available` to find files. Each row is one file, identified by its `file_name` (the name of the archive on the KSJ download site).

```{r}
#| message: false
library(ksjdata)
library(dplyr)

files <- ksj_available |>
  filter(
    dataset_code == "N03",
    year == 2026,
    prefecture_code %in% c("13", "14")
  )
files |>
  select(dataset_name, year_name, area_name, file_name, file_size)
```

Pass a `file_name` to `ksj_get()` to get that file. The first time a dataset is requested in a session, the pages that state its terms of use are shown.

```{r}
ksj_get("N03-20260101_13_GML.zip")
```

To get several files, iterate over their names:

```{r}
#| eval: false
purrr::map(files$file_name, ksj_get)
```

In a [targets](https://docs.ropensci.org/targets/) pipeline, `ksj_target()` declares a target that gets one file. Use `tarchetypes::tar_eval()` to declare one per file.

```{r}
#| eval: false
tarchetypes::tar_eval(
  ksj_target(name, file_name),
  values = list(
    name = rlang::syms(stringr::str_c("n03_", files$prefecture_code)),
    file_name = files$file_name
  )
)
```

The data are returned as published: geometries and coordinate reference systems are not changed, codes keep their leading zeros, and published zeros stay distinct from blank cells (`NA`).

## Terms of use

Each release of a dataset has its own terms, stated on the KSJ site: on the page of the dataset (`page_url` of `ksj_available`) and the pages of its versions, which it links to. The first time a dataset is requested in a session, these pages are shown. Published or processed data must credit the source, and processed data must say that they were processed.

- Terms can differ by release or by area within a dataset: older releases of some datasets cannot be used commercially (非商用) even where the latest is open data, and some areas have their own conditions. Check the terms of the release you use.
- The package does not copy the terms, as the site does not state them in a form that can be read reliably for each file.
- Complying with the terms is up to you. This package does not give legal advice.
- The MIT license of this package applies to its code only, not to the data.

## Supported datasets

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| message: false
library(dplyr)

ksjdata::ksj_available |>
  summarise(
    Name = first(dataset_name),
    Releases = stringr::str_c(min(year), max(year), sep = "–"),
    .by = dataset_code
  ) |>
  arrange(dataset_code) |>
  rename(Code = dataset_code) |>
  knitr::kable()
```
